item.title: 'No one's coming to save us': Nick Sirianni faces questions about Eagles' effort, potential roster losses as NFL trade deadline nears
item.description: As the Philadelphia Eagles’ first loss became their second then third, fourth and now fifth, questions grew. Sure, injuries have contributed heavily to Philadelphia falling at the hands of the Chicago Bears, Los Angeles Rams, Jacksonville Jaguars, Carolina Panthers and Dallas Cowboys. On offense, in particular, half a dozen starters have missed time with multiple expected not to return this season. But a defense that ranked second in points allowed two years ago and fifth last year has fallen to 21st, alongside a bottom-feeding offense. Searching for answers, the questions in a tough media market were likely to go beyond scheme. So head coach Nick Sirianni and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio were each asked this week: Do you have concerns about your players’ effort? “I did not see an effort issue on Monday night,” Sirianni said Wednesday. “Obviously it was other things, which I’m sure you guys will ask me about. There were other things. But effort in no way, shape [or] form was an issue here. “Now, do you bat 100% on effort? No, you don’t play a perfect football game. … But I didn’t [look] at the tape and say, ‘Hey, this was an effort issue.’” Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni and general manager Howie Roseman are looking at a bleak 2026 season. Emilee Chinn via Getty Images Perhaps the Eagles’ 38-21 home loss to Dallas had more to do with a talent deficit than an effort concern. But with 10 games left to play, Sirianni and Co. face a tall task keeping motivated a group that knows quarterback Jalen Hurts isn’t coming back from his blood clots to steady them, and he’s just where the gaps start. Running back Saquon Barkley preached commitment to his team in the postgame locker room Monday. “We’ve been in situations where we won five-plus in a row; now we’re in situations where we lost five in a row,” Barkley told reporters of his message. “The only way we’re going to get out of it is the same way we attacked it when we were winning five in a row. You never give up.” In second half, Eagles have fallen off cliff There’s reason beyond injury to question the Eagles’ ability to rebound this year. item.title: Oldest manager to win first World Series: Where Pat Murphy ranks among elder statesmen in MLB history
item.description: Oldest manager to win first World Series: Where Pat Murphy ranks among elder statesmen in MLB history originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Pat Murphy waited a long time to get his first managerial job, but it was worth the wait. Now, he is a World Series champion. In his third season as the Milwaukee Brewers manager, Murphy has led the team to its first championship in franchise history. Murphy was promoted from bench coach to manager in 2024, a decade after he was the San Diego Padres ' interim manager to end the 2015 season, but this time he earned a permanent fixture. As the sport has begun to skew younger with its managers, Murphy represented a rare instance of a manager getting his first full-time job over the age of 60. With this win, Murphy puts his name among the managers who won it all late in their careers. Most managers who won the World Series later in their lives did so after getting their first titles early on. Murphy, however, is part of a rare group who won their first World Series years into their baseball coaching careers. Here's a look at where Murphy ranks among the oldest World Series managers. MORE : How Brewers built World Series winner on a small-ball budget Oldest manager to win first World Series Dusty Baker holds the record for the oldest manager to win his first World Series, doing so at the age of 73 when he led the Houston Astros to the 2022 World Series title. Baker had been managing for three decades at that point, as he got his start as a manager in 1993, but after making the World Series in 2002, he didn't return to the Fall Classic for another 20 years. Baker broke the record that was once set by Jack McKeon, who led the Florida Marlins to a World Series title in 2003. McKeon was 72 years old at the time and was managing the team on an interim basis after taking over midseason. When the Brewers won the NLCS, Murphy trailed just McKeon as the second-oldest manager to make his World Series debut. At 67 years and 329 days, Pat Murphy is the second-oldest manager in World Series history at the time of his WS debut, younger than only: 2003 Jack McKeon 73y 329d — Sarah Langs (@SlangsOnSports) October 23, 2026 With the Brewers' win, though, Pat Murphy is now third on the list for oldest managers to win their first World Series. He surpasses Brian Snitker, who was 66 when he led the Atlanta Braves to the World Series in 2021. This year's Brewers win also marks the fourth time in six years that an older manager won the World Series. Snitker won in 2021, Baker in 2022, and Bruce Bochy won his fourth World Series in 2023 at the age of 68. After Dave Roberts won two straight titles at 52 and 53, Murphy got his title at 67. item.title: The Brewers Just Won The World Series. Here’s How Their Owner Made His Fortune.
item.description: Mark Attanasio waited more than two decades for this moment. So after an agonizing 12-inning loss in Game 4, what was one more night? On Wednesday at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida—44 years after their only previous World Series appearance—the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays, 4-1, in Game 5 to deliver the franchise’s first championship. In the middle of the celebration was the 69-year-old Attanasio, who bought the team in 2005 and couldn’t help grinning from ear to ear as he hoisted the Commissioner’s Trophy. “Milwaukee has waited 44 years, and Milwaukee, you have your world championship!” Attanasio said from the on-field stage, surrounded by Brewers players, coaches and executives. “I know that we’ve got tens of thousands of fans at American Family Field—we appreciate that you’ve all been with us the whole way, and everyone in the state of Wisconsin has gotten behind us.” The title caps off an already-remarkable season for the Brewers, who won a franchise-record 103 games during the regular season and then swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series to avenge a loss to the same team in the same round a year earlier. Milwaukee didn’t need the spending power of the Dodgers to do it, either. Playing in the country’s 41st-largest metropolitan area, the Brewers had a $146 million payroll this season, ranking 19th among MLB’s 30 teams, according to Spotrac. Forbes That fact—along with the World Series appearance by the Rays, whose payroll ranked 28th—adds an interesting twist to the financial debate set to embroil baseball as the league’s collective bargaining agreement with its players expires in December. Team owners— including Attanasio —are pushing for a salary cap that they argue is necessary to improve the league’s competitive balance. But their real motivation, the players’ union says, is that the proposal would drive up franchise values. Not that the current system has prevented owners from profiting. Attanasio, for instance, bought the Brewers for $223 million ($394 million in today’s dollars), and 21 years later, Forbes values the franchise at $1.9 billion, No. 21 among MLB’s 30 teams . Meanwhile, Attanasio, who owns an estimated 45% stake in the team, has amassed a personal fortune of $1.9 billion , according to Forbes estimates. His path to billionaire status wasn’t the most straightforward. After graduating from Columbia Law School in 1982, Attanasio joined the New York-based firm Debevoise & Plimpton, but three years in, he had little interest in the climb toward partnership and left for a career in investment banking. Moving to California, he joined Drexel Burnham Lambert, the Wall Street bank that helped popularize junk bonds, and worked in mergers and acquisitions before turning to trading. item.title: Brewers defeat Rays in 5 games to win first World Series in franchise history
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are finally World Series champions after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday night, taking the series 4-1. Wednesday's 4-1 win at Tropicana Field in Tampa gave the Brewers their first title since their founding as an expansion franchise 57 years ago. It was just their second trip to the World Series, with the first appearance coming in 1982, when they fell to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games. Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings of two-hit ball and rookie Cooper Pratt got two more hits and two RBIs to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field. "It's the best feeling ever. All of our fans are here. I know the city's waited a long, long time for this," Milwaukee captain Christian Yelich said. "We're so happy to bring it home to them. I can't wait to get back there and celebrate." Misiorowski left the game because of a right calf cramp. He got a standing ovation from the Brew-Crew fans, who took over the section behind Milwaukee's dugout for the last three games. The 22-year-old Pratt set a Series rookie record with six straight hits before a sacrifice fly in the sixth inning. Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits. "This is one of the greatest moments of my life. Oh my gosh. It doesn't even feel real," said Pratt, who made his major league debut in June. "This is surreal. It only took four months!" The Rays, also an expansion team, though from 1998, were seeking their first World Series championship as well, but the odds were stacked against the American League champions after falling behind 3-0 in the best-of-seven series. They were able to scratch out just one win with a dramatic come-from-behind 4-3 victory in the 12th inning of Game Four on Tuesday to avoid getting swept, but the Brewers finished the job the next night. Pat Murphy's team displayed the resilience of the 67-year-old manager, who survived a heart attack in 2020 and was the NL Manager of the Year in his first two full seasons at the helm in 2024 and 2025. With their flame-throwing, 24-year-old two-time All-Star on the mound, the Brewers rebounded from Game 4. "I don't even have words," Misiorowski said. "It's amazing, just watching my guys celebrate. And the city — I know they're going crazy in Milwaukee. It's awesome." item.title: How Beechwood, Notre Dame advanced to Ninth Region volleyball final
item.description: The 2026 Ninth Region volleyball champion will come from the 35th District. It's been an exciting regional tournament over three days at Dayton High School but there hasn't been a whole lot of drama. Five of the first six matches have been sweeps. No matter what happens on Oct. 29, the matchup between state No. 2 Notre Dame and No. 4 Beechwood will be a fitting end to the season as it relates to Northern Kentucky. Either the Pandas or Tigers will be a worthy representative at next week's state tournament. Here's what happened in Wendesday night's regional semifinals. Beechwood sweeps Conner, advances to first regional championship since 2003 Behind 16 kills from newly-minted Ninth Region Player of the Year Isabel O'Brien, the Beechwood Tigers swept the Conner Cougars 25-18, 25-17, 25-19 to extend their season at least one more day and earn a berth in their first regional championship in 23 years. They are also the first public school to play for the region title since 2022. Since the start of the century, Beechwood, Scott, Simon Kenton, Cooper and Ryle have been the only public schools to advance to the championship match. Head coach Matt Long continues to preach to his team the importance of playing a full game, and that's what the Tigers did on Wednesday night. They were aggressive at the service line, on the attack, and they played exceptional back line defense to shut down the Cougars. "We've had some big roles that we had to fill this past year because we lost four seniors. Our younger girls have done nothing but excel and I'm just so proud of them. Our team chemistry's amazing, everyone's so fun and we enjoy being around each other," O'Brien said. Despite 10 hitting errors and eight service errors, Beechwood's experience prevailed as the girls used runs in each set to pull away. With the first set tied at 13, a Macy Armstrong kill kickstarted a 12-5 run for the 1-0 lead. Three Conner errors put the Cougars in a four-point hole to start the second set before O'Brien, Armstrong and Skylr Estep were the catalysts for two four-point runs to take a 19-10 lead. "It's been kind of prevalent throughout the tournament, where we're starting a little tight with a little too much pressure on ourselves. I talk to them in timeouts: 'Take a deep breath. Relax, enjoy, play together but don't play tight.'" Long said. The Tigers opened up a 17-12 lead in the third set before the Cougars clawed back to get within 22-19 behind kills from Skylyn Koerber, Olivia Borneman and Charlotte Patton. For the majority of the match, taking the ball out of Conner's hitters' hands was the game plan for Beechwood. Patton, who had 511 kills in the regular season, posted just seven, five of which came in the final set. Koerber and Borneman picked up the slack, totaling 11 teminations. item.title: Austin FC eliminated from MLS playoff race with loss to Real Salt Lake
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 19: Jorge Alastuey #24 of the Austin FC dribbles the ball and looks to pass during the first half against the Seattle Sounders FC at Lumen Field on August 19, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Blake Dahlin/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) (Blake Dahlin/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Austin FC can start looking to the 2027 MLS sprint season. The Verde and Black were officially eliminated from the playoff race Wednesday with a 2-1 loss to Real Salt Lake at Q2 Stadium. Jorge Alastuey's first career goal on a brilliant strike early in the second half gave Austin FC a brief lead, but the visitors scored twice in the following nine minutes to take control as Saba Lobjanidze hit a curling shot in the box and Morgan Guilavogui finished a counterattack. With two games remaining, Austin FC (8-14-10, 34 points) can only finish with 40 points, which is two points behind the current ninth-place team in the Western Conference, Colorado. item.description: Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Hornets’ Charles Lee reveals why Naz Reid didn’t play in the second half vs. Pistons appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Naz Reid entered the Charlotte Hornets ’ Wednesday night clash against the Detroit Pistons as the team’s second-leading scorer , being every bit as good as advertised after coming over in the LaMelo Ball trade this past offseason. However, Reid found himself in head coach Charles Lee’s doghouse for the entire second half of what would be a 97-89 loss to the Pistons, raising a few eyebrows in the process. Reid played 12 minutes and 42 seconds in the first half and didn’t see the floor for a single second following the halftime break. Lee clarified that the Hornets big man’s absence during the second half wasn’t injury-related, saying that Reid simply did not play up to the team’s standards and got himself benched for it. “Unfortunately, Naz didn’t meet our standards in the first half, and at halftime, we made the decision that he wouldn’t play in the second half. But I look forward to him meeting those standards come next game,” Lee said after the game on DAZN, via Hornets Reddit on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "Unfortunately, Naz didn't meet our standards in the first half, and at halftime we made the decision that he wouldn't play in the second half." Charles Lee on why Naz Reid didn't play in the second half 🗣️ (via @hornets ) pic.twitter.com/bY41DZ9Ier — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 29, 2026 It’s not quite clear what Reid did or did not do that landed him in the Hornets head coach’s doghouse. After putting up seven points and six boards in the first half, one would think that Charlotte could have used him out there on the court to get more of an offensive punch against an elite defensive team such as the Pistons. But perhaps Reid missed a few defensive assignments or didn’t play within the team’s system, generally-speaking. Nonetheless, this Hornets team was already missing Coby White and Kon Knueppel , and benching Reid meant that Brandon Miller had to carry the offensive load on his own. For Lee, however, it’s important to establish his authority and make sure that players meet the standards the Hornets are setting behind the scenes. No one is above the team, and that is the message Lee wants his players to know moving forward. item.description: Who won World Series MVP in 2026? How William Contreras led the Brewers to a championship originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Brewers' reputation entering 2026 was that of a well-run franchise with a small budget that simply didn't have the star power to match the big guns of the Dodgers and other higher-payroll teams in the postseason. Narratives are meant to be shattered, though. That's exactly what Milwaukee did this October. The Brewers captured their first championship, dispatching the Padres, Dodgers and Rays en route to the World Series title. Manager Pat Murphy would be the first to say the history-making run was possible because the Brewers play as a true team, but only one player could be honored with the 2026 World Series MVP award. Here's a look at which Brewer was named World Series MVP after sweeping the Rays. MORE: How Brewers built World Series team with low budget Who won World Series MVP? Brewers catcher William Contreras won World Series MVP, becoming the first catcher to receive the honor since Salvador Perez in 2015 and the eighth catcher to do so in World Series history. Contreras, who beat out Jackson Chourio and Cooper Pratt for the award, went 8-for-21 (.381) in the series, driving in four runs and stealing one base but not hitting any home runs. While the award is specifically for the World Series, Contreras had a stellar postseason with 19 hits and three home runs for an OPS north of 1.000. item.title: William Contreras’ journey from Venezuela to World Series MVP
item.description: William Contreras’ journey from Venezuela to World Series MVP originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . William Contreras’ World Series MVP story began nowhere near a major league stadium. It began in Puerto Cabello, Venezuela, where he played baseball with his brothers using balls made from wadded paper and tape. As a kid, Contreras was an infielder. He played shortstop and second base, positions where he could stay involved in every play. Then, at 17, he signed with the Atlanta Braves for $10,000 and moved behind the plate. The change became the defining decision of his career. Contreras came to love catching for the responsibility it carried. “I love being in the middle of the field,” he said. “I love being the only person who has everybody in front of you.” For a young player who had spent years focused on hitting, learning to manage pitchers and control a game from behind the plate demanded a new kind of work. A catcher’s job is bigger than the box score Contreras made his major league debut with Atlanta in 2020. item.description: Feb 9, 2025; New Orleans, LA, USA; Fox Sports sideline reporter Erin Andrews during the Kansas City Chiefs game against the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl LIX at Ceasars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Erin Andrews was on the sideline for Fox during Sunday’s game between the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions at Ford Field. And while she had a productive halftime conversation with Packers head coach Matt LaFleur, the report that followed didn’t exactly go according to plan. On the latest episode of her Calm Down podcast with Charissa Thompson, Andrews explained how a long walk, a short clock, and a missing injury update left her out of breath on live television, calling the moment “inappropriate” and admitting that she was hard on herself afterward. ‘I never want to misquote’ Andrews said that she usually only has time for a couple of questions with a head coach at halftime. But because the ramp at Ford Field is so long, she got much more time with LaFleur than usual, leaving her with only about a minute before going back on the air. “I’m like, ‘Oh my God, I’ve got to shore up my notes.’ I’m putting it all together,” Andrews said, via Awful Announcing . “And I’m like, ‘Wait, [expletive]. What did he say about going for it?’ Because I never want to quote a coach and get it wrong.” Andrews explained that she records her conversations with coaches so that she can listen back to their exact words. “I’ve started to do it the last couple of years just because there may be something they say, and I want to get it exactly right,” Andrews said. “I never want to misquote.” That’s an interesting answer, considering Thompson claimed back in 2023 that she used to make up reports as a sideline reporter, comments she later tried to walk back amid plenty of backlash. ‘Out of breath’ Moments before going on the air, Andrews said that she realized she still needed Green Bay’s injury updates. “So, I run. item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL. – When the Milwaukee Brewers needed him most, Jacob Misiorowski was there for them. The right-hander turned in a strong 5 ⅔-inning despite a game-long battle with the mound conditions before departing after throwing his 86th pitch with cramping in his right calf. It was just what the doctor ordered for a team that had used all its key relievers a night earlier in what ended up being a 12-inning loss and set the stage for a 4-0 Game 5 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays that clinched Milwaukee's first World Series title at Tropicana Field on Wednesday, Oct. 28. Misiorowski entered the game on the heels of a trio of subpar performances – at least by the high standards set by the odds-on favorite to be named the National League Cy Young Award winner next month – that had seen the opposition run up his pitch count early and limit his overall effectiveness. Sporting a 1-0 record and 2.70 ERA, Misiorowski took the mound opposite Drew Rasmussen, who was pitching on short rest for the Rays with their season on the line. It was apparent early that Misiorowski was on his game while also employing something of a different game plan than in previous starts – pitching to contact rather than the strikeout-centric approach that's defined his career to this point. Misiorowski's signature fastball was still in full effect, however, with each of his first 11 pitches – all fastballs – clocking in at least 100.9 mph and topping out at 103. He was only eight pitches into the night when the mound first became an issue, with Misiorowski kicking at his landing spot after slipping on a follow-through. The grounds crew quickly filled in the divot, a procedure that became an every-inning endeavor for the rest of Misiorowski's outing. item.description: Sergio Pérez has made a decision many drivers at his age and stage would not have considered. At 36 years old, with six victories and 39 podiums to his name, the Mexican has signed a multi-year contract extension with Cadillac , the team that currently occupies the last position on the grid and is far from seeking a seat in a top team that would allow him to fight for victories immediately; Pérez has opted for faith in a project that is still in its infancy, a bet that says a lot about his character and his confidence in himself. His on-track performance has been hard to measure because of the car's limitations, but within Cadillac and in his own environment, there is consensus: the Mexican is driving at an extraordinary level. Bob Uecker wasn’t in the radio booth to call the final out, but it is hard to tell the story of the team without hearing his voice in it. Uecker was born in Milwaukee in 1934. Before he became “Mr. Baseball,” he was a hometown kid who signed with the Milwaukee Braves, worked his way through the minors and reached the major leagues in 1962. He played six seasons as a catcher for the Braves, St. Louis Cardinals and Philadelphia Phillies , hitting .200 with 14 home runs. His statistics were modest. His place in baseball history would not be. Uecker did win a World Series as a player. He was a reserve catcher on the 1964 Cardinals, who beat the Yankees in seven games. Uecker turned his playing struggles into comedy, but the joke was never the whole story. He understood baseball from behind the plate, and the National Baseball Hall of Fame recognized his broadcasting with the 2003 Ford C. Frick Award. He joined the Brewers’ radio team in 1971 and called games for his hometown club through the 2024 season, completing 54 years in the booth. item.description: Carles Gil’s historic milestone helps push New England into 2nd in East By Harrison Hamm Carles Gil ’s place in New England Revolution history is secure. The Revs captain recorded his 100th career MLS regular-season assist in a 3-2 victory over Red Bull New York at Gillette Stadium. The Spanish playmaker became just the eighth player in league history to reach the milestone. The achievement only adds to Gil’s list of accomplishments in New England. item.title: Brewers beat Rays 4-1 to capture first World Series title
item.description: Milwaukee's Cooper Pratt scores a run in the Brewers' World Series-clinching win over the Tampa Bay Rays (ELSA) The Milwaukee Brewers won the first World Series title in franchise history on Wednesday, beating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 to clinch victory in Major League Baseball's championship showcase. Rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt drove in one run, plated another with a sacrifice fly and scored as the Brewers -- denied a sweep by the Rays' thrilling extra-innings comeback win on Tuesday -- celebrated a four games to one victory in the best-of-seven series at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. Milwaukee's first World Series title comes 44 years after their only other trip to the Fall Classic, when they lost to St. Louis in seven games in 1982. The Brewers, who swept the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, gained an early 1-0 edge on Pratt's single to center field that scored Brice Turang in the top of the second inning. Pratt was cut down trying to reach second base and the Rays escaped the inning without further damage. Pratt singled again -- his sixth hit in six straight at-bats -- and scored on David Hamilton's single up the middle as the Brewers doubled their lead in the top of the fifth. Milwaukee added two more runs for a 4-0 lead in the sixth, when Rays reliever Garrett Cleavinger hit Christian Yelich to open the inning. William Contreras followed with a double to left field that scored Yelich. After Turang belted a single Tyler Wells took the mound for Tampa Bay. He struck out Sal Frelick before Pratt lofted a sacrifice fly to right field that allowed Contreras to score. Milwaukee's flame-throwing pitching ace Jacob Misiorowski, who led the major leagues with 252 strikeouts in the regular season, recorded just two. But he pitched five and two-thirds scoreless innings, giving up just two hits before exiting with apparent leg cramps. Misiorowski didn't get his first strikeout of the game until the fourth inning. He then gave up a two-out single to Chandler Simpson, who reached second on a fielding error by Sal Frelick as Liam Hicks -- who had reached first when he was hit by a Misiorowski pitch -- advanced to third. Misiorowski escaped the jam when Ben Williamson grounded out to third to strand the Rays runners in scoring position. Trailing by four runs, the Rays got a glimmer of a chance in the bottom of the seventh when Chandler Simpson's one-out chopper was mis-handled by Brewers catcher Contreras, whose high throw down the right field line allowed Simpson to make it to second base. Simpson reached third base on Richie Palacios's ground out, but Brewers reliever Abner Uribe retired Victor Mesa Jr. to end the threat. Simpson drove in the Rays' only run, with a double in the bottom of the ninth, but there would be no miracle comeback and the Rays remain in search of a first title, having now come up empty in three World Series appearances. bb/amz
